get.summary: What's Hot Right Now — a ranked, significance-filtered list of noteworthy MLB events (live-game situations for now; never padded to a target count).
Today's line for each followed team/player — a dashboard row, not a feed. Identity is device-local; the client sends its own follow list every call.

Races — divisions and wild card, a fixed set of eight team races every day, each compressed to a clinched leader once decided. Chases (individual leaders) travel in the same response but render as their own section. Six division one-liners only in early season (a games-remaining condition, not a date).

Postseason bracket — replaces Races once all 12 berths are clinched (a condition, not a date). Seven rounds with seeds, series wins and card state, plus every game of each started series for the series drawer (score, W/L/SV, notable line, recap video).
Today's shortlist — up to four games picked by a lower-bar significance heuristic (race stakes, rivalry), never the first four by start time. Real totalCount for "All N games today".

detailedState.description: Provider detailed state (e.g., Delayed, Postponed, Suspended). Useful for edge statuses.

currentInning.description: Current inning number (alias used by some provider feeds)

question.example: What team is Mauricio Dubon on?

sub.example: Mauricio Dubon plays for the Houston Astros.

updateIndex.description: Which moment the user is asking from — required, since review mode may be earlier than live. -1 is valid and means no play has happened yet (Scout paused at marker 0, or pregame).

question.example: Would that last hit be out in other parks?

conversationHistory.description: Prior turns from this same panel session, oldest first — lets a follow-up question ("wasn't he traded?") resolve against what was already asked/answered.

value.description: Pre-formatted with units — the client does no number formatting.

ok.description: False when no real answer could be produced (bad gameId, no history yet, Claude unavailable, etc.) — the client should render its designed "unavailable" state rather than sniffing headline/sub text.

headline.description: Short, mono, usually numeric — rendered at 30px, not a sentence.

sub.example: Suzuki's single to right field (104.1 mph, 12° launch) clears the wall in 22 of 30 parks.

ok.description: false when the upstream people lookup failed

status.description: Upstream HTTP status, only when ok is false

battingAverage.description: The player's batting average for the season.

onBasePercentage.description: The player's on-base percentage for the season.

sluggingPercentage.description: The player's slugging percentage for the season.

onBasePlusSlugging.description: The player's OPS for the season.

homeRuns.description: The player's home runs for the season.

runsBattedIn.description: The player's runs batted in for the season.

statLine.description: The stat line for today's stats.

isLive.description: Whether the player is currently in a live game.

season.description: The season for which the stats are displayed.

headline.description: The player's headline stats for the season.

secondary.description: The player's secondary stats for the season.

runningAvg.description: Running season-to-date batting average through this game (Σhits / ΣatBats, chronological order). Null when ΣatBats === 0.

hr.description: Career home runs in this matchup

pa.description: Career plate appearances in this matchup

isFinal.description: A final game renders "Final", never a live inning arrow.

type.description: NO_HIT_BID | PERFECT_GAME_BID | NO_HITTER_COMPLETED | PERFECT_GAME_COMPLETED | CYCLE_BID | CYCLE_COMPLETED | MULTI_HOME_RUN_GAME | HIGH_LEVERAGE_LATE

headline.example: Hunter Brown (HOU) has a no-hitter through six innings.
headline.description: Display-ready prose, composed server-side — never assembled by the client.

hasIqContext.description: Real availability flag resolved server-side — the client must not infer this from event type. true = show the red diamond bullet; false = the plain dot.

iqSuggested.description: Static suggested-question prompts for this event type — not a fabricated answer.

lines.description: Exactly two content lines; the card renders them at a fixed height.

id.description: Team abbreviation, or player mlbId as a string.

state.description: Decides the tile's leading-edge color only — the state itself is folded into each face.

faces.description: TODAY, SEASON, then NEXT GAME when there is a game today. The client cycles them.

wl.description: Optional win-loss note; column drops entirely when absent.

gamesBack.description: "-" for the leader, "IN" for a clinched wild-card spot (never a bare number/glyph).

holdingSpot.description: Wild card only — inside the cut line.

mode.description: early = six division one-liners only, no wild card/chases (condition-gated, not calendar-gated).

note.example: 9 games left in the regular season

options.description: One of two possible clubs (a logo pair) before the feeding series is decided.

label.description: A word when not even the candidates are known.

seed.description: Derived from the bracket structure; MLB publishes none.

startTime.description: ISO start; null while MLB lists the time as TBD.

note.description: multi-HR > HR + RBI > 3+ hits > pitcher ≥7 IP or ≥10 K; null when nothing qualifies.

active.description: All 12 berths clinched (or the postseason under way) — a condition, not a date.

stake.description: A real, checkable reason this game made the shortlist. Never fabricated.

totalCount.description: Real total for "All N games today →".

clinchIndicator.description: MLB's own authoritative clinch marker for this team — 'y' division, 'x' wild card/playoff berth, 'z' bye/home field, null if nothing clinched yet. Not derived locally.

winsByDay.description: Cumulative wins as of each date the team played a completed game. Sparse — one entry per game date, not per calendar day.

atBatIndex.description: null when unmatched to a play (§6a).

description.example: Connor Wong lines a go-ahead double to left field to give the Red Sox a 4-3 lead in the bottom of the 7th inning
